title: Execute locked filesystem and Paseo provider transactions
description:
## Objective
Compose planned file operations and one three-provider daemon patch under a deterministic per-user daemon/provider lock, with verification, manifest commit, and reverse compensation.

## Context
Different room roots and endpoint aliases target the same provider IDs; only one can claim them, and filesystem plus daemon changes are not ACID.

## Scope
In scope:
- Global `/tmp/paseo-room-<uid>` lock, stale-owner validation, local-admission recheck, active-session refusal, transaction state machine, provider patch/read-back/refresh, manifest commit.
Out of scope:
- Interrupted-journal recovery UI and partial uninstall cleanup.

## Components Touched
- Transaction orchestrator, lock implementation, Paseo gateway integration, manifest writer, concurrency tests.

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- Private journal/file primitives and live Paseo provider verification must exist.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- Lock key is SHA-256 of canonical local Paseo home, normalized status listen endpoint, and fixed provider namespace only; room root, endpoint spelling, TMPDIR, and XDG variables cannot split it.
- Re-read local home/PID/UID/listen admission and current providers after lock. Refuse non-terminal managed sessions. No automatic mutation retry.
- Install/update commit is atomic manifest with matching transaction ID; failed verification compensates conditionally.

## Risks / Gotchas
- External same-ID writers are unsupported; visible divergence must become recovery-required, never trigger whole-config restore.

## Validation / Definition of Done
- Two processes using distinct roots, endpoint aliases, and environment paths admit exactly one provider owner.
- Injected failures around daemon patch/refresh/verify/manifest commit reach old committed, new committed, or recovery-required state.
- Successful apply creates exactly three ready profiles and second apply performs no mutation.

## Primary Proof
Concurrency plus cross-filesystem/daemon fault-injection integration suite using fakes and isolated daemon.

## Reversibility
Before-values and file before-images compensate only owned after-values; divergence remains preserved with journal evidence under the R3 containment policy.

## Provenance
Source: docs/plans/paseo-room-phase-1-implementation-plan.md#wp-005-transaction-global-lock-rollback-and-recovery
Requirements: REQ-003, REQ-006, REQ-011, REQ-012, REQ-014
Design refs: docs/design/platform/paseo-room.md#72-apply-and-rollback-flow; docs/design/platform/paseo-room.md#73-locking-and-idempotency; docs/design/platform/paseo-room.md#r3-decision
notes: DONE 2026-09-09: Added deterministic owner-only global lock keyed solely by canonical Paseo home, normalized loopback listen and fixed provider namespace; PID/start evidence fails closed for busy/stale/unsafe ownership. Added journal-bound no-clobber manifest commit, transaction orchestrator, public-SDK transaction gateway and committed cleanup. Executor rechecks admission/providers/sessions under lock, publishes files, issues one complete patch, performs full readback/refresh/readiness/policy/file verification, and commits a same-ID manifest. Conditional reversal preserves unrelated/divergent providers/files; unresolved forward/reverse RPCs and failed restored-registry verification retain recovery evidence. R2 findings remediated; final independent review PASS. Verified npm run verify: typecheck, lint, 17 files/1022 tests, build, pack and package test. Isolated Paseo 0.8.0-beta.1 contract: 2/2 unauthenticated/authenticated cases passed. Cross-process lock proof uses an acquisition barrier and distinct room roots/endpoint spelling/TMPDIR/XDG.
close_reason: DoD verified: locked end-to-end install/update transaction, crash-safe manifest commit, conditional compensation, concurrency proof, R2 PASS, full and isolated gates green

title: Document installation, ownership, recovery, and release checks
description:
## Objective
Write operator documentation and a traceable Phase 1 acceptance/release checklist matching the implemented packed CLI behavior.

## Context
Users own Paseo/Codex and need truthful prerequisites, dry-run/apply usage, capability limits, recovery, drift, modified-file preservation, and uninstall guidance.

## Scope
In scope:
- README/operations docs for commands/options, macOS/Linux prerequisites, Paseo >=0.8.0-beta.1, role topology/policy, paths/manifest, errors, recovery, uninstall, security caveat, and reference-install conflict.
- REQ-001–REQ-016 evidence matrix and R3 rehearsal procedure.
Out of scope:
- Later agent adapters, Windows, npm publication, and executing real-home rehearsal.

## Components Touched
- `README.md`, `docs/operations/`, and release/acceptance evidence document.

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- Automated Linux/macOS behavior and smoke results must be final so documentation cannot speculate.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- State clearly that Peer policy is not OS sandboxing and CLI never installs/manages Paseo.
- Never include credentials, private paths, or copied reference prose.
- Unscoped package name is `paseo-room`; fallback scope only if npm availability changes before publish.

## Validation / Definition of Done
- Every command/flag/outcome/exit code matches black-box help and tests.
- Link/check scripts pass; all Phase 1 requirements map to evidence.
- R3 procedure includes explicit approval, checksums/backups, no credential copying, verification, and cleanup/rollback.

## Primary Proof
Documentation contract check against CLI help/JSON schemas plus complete REQ acceptance matrix review.

## Reversibility
Documentation-only repository change; no external state.

## Provenance
Source: docs/plans/paseo-room-phase-1-implementation-plan.md#wp-007-cross-component-acceptance-and-release-hardening
Requirements: REQ-001 through REQ-016
Design refs: docs/design/platform/paseo-room.md#4-public-cli-contract; docs/design/platform/paseo-room.md#11-backward-compatibility-migration-and-rollback; docs/design/platform/paseo-room.md#r3-decision
notes: DONE 2026-09-10: Added operator guide and Phase 1 acceptance/release record. Documented exact commands/options/outcomes/exits, platform/dependency prerequisites, ownership/security limits, drift/reapply, recovery, residual uninstall, and non-adoption/manual handling for reference-install conflicts. Added REQ-001–REQ-016 evidence matrix linked to hosted run 34426300649. Added approval-gated R3 procedure with credential exclusions, limited private backups, dry-run/apply/no-op/uninstall/conditional recovery, sanitized evidence, and explicit pending release status. Updated README/internal CLI docs and added automated local-link/public-contract checks. R2 PASS; typecheck/lint/docs 5/5 and diff-check pass.

title: Run the full automated suite on Linux and macOS
description:

title: Implement manifest v1 and owned-state observation
description:
## Objective
Implement validated manifest v1 persistence models and read-only observation/comparison of owned files, links, directories, provider entries, source drift, and residual uninstall state.

## Context
Update/uninstall must reconstruct ownership without adopting collisions, hashing credentials, following links, or deleting Codex-created mutable state.

## Scope
In scope:
- `src/core/manifest.ts`, canonical JSON/SHA-256 helpers, artifact observation, manifest load/validation, and source/provider binding.
- committed and uninstall-incomplete statuses.
Out of scope:
- Writing manifests inside a transaction and deciding operation ordering.

## Components Touched
- Core manifest/schema/hash/path modules and fixture tests.

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- Codex artifact declarations and Paseo live/provider facts must be complete.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- Unknown schema versions fail read-only. Credential content/hash is forbidden. Symlink comparison uses literal target/type and `lstat`.
- Manifest is bound to package/adapter, canonical source, Codex prefix, and verified Paseo endpoint identity derived from canonical local home and normalized status listen endpoint.

## Risks / Gotchas
- Role directories contain unowned mutable state and cannot be recursively owned or deleted.

## Validation / Definition of Done
- Schemas accept all design states and reject malformed/unknown versions.
- Comparison detects unchanged/customized/missing/wrong-type artifacts and fixed-shape provider drift.
- Auth links are never dereferenced or hashed; mutable extra children remain unowned.

## Primary Proof
Manifest schema and owned-state fixture suite, including malicious link/path cases.

## Reversibility
This leaf reads only; repository changes can be reverted. Future persisted writes are transaction-controlled.

## Provenance
Source: docs/plans/paseo-room-phase-1-implementation-plan.md#wp-004-desired-state-planner-and-ownership-manifest
Requirements: REQ-012, REQ-014
Design refs: docs/design/platform/paseo-room.md#3-persistent-data-model; docs/design/platform/paseo-room.md#71-planning-and-ownership
notes: DONE 2026-09-09: Implemented strict manifest v1 schema/build/load, canonical JSON/SHA256, endpoint/source/provider bindings, residual ownership subsets, and deterministic read-only observation. R2 found missing symlink mode and path-race exposure; fixed with persisted 0777 symlink mode and cwd-anchored child hashing that validates previously accepted parent plus leaf descriptor before reading and returns digest only. Final R2 PASS. Verified npm run verify (547 tests, build, pack, package); focused 129. macOS live race proof passed; Linux live remains later CI evidence.
close_reason: Definition of Done verified; final R2 approved after race-safe hashing remediation

title: Execute the owner-approved macOS user-home R3 rehearsal
description:
## Objective
Execute and record the final owner-approved macOS user-home install/update/verify/uninstall rehearsal using the packed artifact and the documented R3 controls.

## Context
This distinct rollout evidence is mandatory before Phase 1 release because disposable fixtures cannot fully prove interaction with the operator-managed local daemon and canonical Codex resources.

## Scope
In scope:
- Request explicit owner approval at execution time; capture pre-state/checksums and managed backups; dry-run review; apply/verify/no-op update; safe uninstall or rollback; record sanitized evidence.
Out of scope:
- Npm publication, credential copying, force deletion, daemon installation/upgrade/management, or bypassing failed checks.

## Components Touched
- Operator's approved macOS environment only after confirmation; release evidence record.

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- Operator documentation and all automated/platform gates must be complete and green.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- This bead is blocked until the repository owner explicitly approves the exact rehearsal target and window.
- Never print/copy/hash credential content; canonical Codex bytes must remain unchanged except writes independently made by running Codex through approved shared links.
- Abort before apply on mismatch/conflict; use conditional rollback, never blind backup restore.

## Risks / Gotchas
- This is the only authorized real user-home mutation in Phase 1 and is governed by the Active design R3 decision. External same-ID writes during the window are unsupported.

## Validation / Definition of Done
- Pre/post canonical checksums, managed provider policy, role readiness, idempotent second apply, and cleanup/uninstall are recorded without secrets.
- Any divergence is preserved as recovery-required and resolved under owner direction; no release approval while unresolved.
- The acceptance matrix links the sanitized rehearsal result.

## Primary Proof
Owner-approved signed-off rehearsal record plus packed CLI outputs and pre/post ownership/checksum evidence.

## Reversibility
Use manifest/journal conditional compensation and documented backups. No irreversible point is accepted; stop and preserve evidence on divergence.

## Provenance
Source: docs/plans/paseo-room-phase-1-implementation-plan.md#wp-007-cross-component-acceptance-and-release-hardening
Requirements: REQ-004, REQ-005, REQ-006, REQ-008, REQ-011, REQ-012, REQ-013, REQ-016

title: Discover safe Codex launch prefixes and canonical homes
description:
## Objective
Implement read-only Codex discovery that returns a validated native `[absoluteCodex]` or npm `[absoluteNode, absoluteCodexScript]` launch prefix and a safe canonical Codex home.

## Context
Paseo GUI environments cannot rely on shell PATH, and the installer must never write inside canonical Codex state or allow nested managed roots.

## Scope
In scope:
- `src/adapters/codex/discover.ts` and path/process helpers.
- Explicit flag, environment, and default precedence; version/model command probes.
- Bidirectional root separation and shared-target containment checks.
Out of scope:
- TOML rendering and filesystem publication.

## Components Touched
- Codex discovery, process runner, and `src/core/paths.ts`.
- Native executable, Node shebang, unsupported shebang, symlink, nested-root, and paths-with-spaces fixtures.

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- Stable intent and adapter contracts must exist.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- Use argv arrays with `shell:false` and timeouts.
- Other interpreter/shell launchers fail closed. Resolve aliases with realpath; canonical and managed roots cannot contain one another.
- Discovery never creates files and never logs secrets.

## Risks / Gotchas
- Version-manager symlinks can move; manifest drift is handled later by doctor/re-apply.

## Validation / Definition of Done
- Native and npm launcher fixtures return expected absolute prefixes and versions.
- Unsupported launchers, missing config/auth, target escape, and either nested-root direction fail with actionable checks.
- Canonical fixture bytes and filesystem tree remain unchanged.

## Primary Proof
Focused discovery/path security tests using temporary homes and minimal process environments.

## Reversibility
Read-only implementation; repository changes can be reverted with no external state.

## Provenance
Source: docs/plans/paseo-room-phase-1-implementation-plan.md#wp-002-codex-discovery-and-role-runtime-adapter
Requirements: REQ-004, REQ-009, REQ-016
Design refs: docs/design/platform/paseo-room.md#52-codex; docs/design/platform/paseo-room.md#6-security
close_reason: Implemented read-only Codex home/launch discovery with precedence, native/npm absolute prefixes, bounded sanitized probes, bidirectional root separation, symlink/path/hardlink controls, resource containment, and credential inode/device alias rejection before reads. Validated: typecheck; lint; 28 focused cases within 192 passing unit tests; build; pack dry-run; packed CLI tests. Risk R2 security: independent Oracle review found credential-alias gap; fixed with negative config/Codex/Node alias tests and full gate rerun. Real Codex smoke remains downstream.

title: Probe and connect to a compatible local Paseo daemon
description:
## Objective
Implement a read-only Paseo CLI/daemon probe and authenticated public SDK connection that proves a locally admitted daemon and version >=0.8.0-beta.1.

## Context
Paseo is user-owned; apply must fail before mutation when CLI/local home/PID/UID/listen admission, version, reachability, or authentication is incompatible.

## Scope
In scope:
- `src/paseo/cli-probe.ts`, gateway connection lifecycle, status JSON validation, semver, canonical local-home resolution, current-user PID/owner evidence, and normalized loopback listen matching.
- PASEO_PASSWORD in-memory handling and timeouts.
Out of scope:
- Installing/starting/upgrading Paseo and provider mutation.

## Components Touched
- Paseo process probe, public `createPaseoClient` wrapper, schemas, and fake CLI/SDK tests.

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- Stable result/gateway interfaces must exist.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- Node >=22; import only `@getpaseo/client` public root.
- CLI and daemon versions must be valid, equal after normalization, and at the floor. Remote targets and local home/listen/owner mismatches are rejected. Connected-peer identity is not claimed because it is unavailable from the pinned public SDK.
- Password is never accepted as a flag, logged, persisted, or forwarded to Codex/provider environments; when present it is passed in memory only to the selected Paseo status subprocess environment and public SDK config.

## Validation / Definition of Done
- Tests classify missing, stopped, unreachable, auth-required/failed, old, version-mismatched, remote, local-home/listen/owner-mismatched, and compatible cases.
- Client always closes in `finally`; read probes have bounded timeout/retry.
- Secret-redaction tests cover thrown errors and result rendering.

## Primary Proof
Fake CLI/SDK integration tests plus a successful isolated v0.8.0-beta.1 daemon handshake.

## Reversibility
Read-only gateway; no external mutation. Repository code can be reverted.

## Provenance
Source: docs/plans/paseo-room-phase-1-implementation-plan.md#wp-003-paseo-compatibility-gateway-and-provider-policy
Requirements: REQ-005, REQ-016
Design refs: docs/design/platform/paseo-room.md#51-paseo; docs/design/platform/paseo-room.md#82-apply-with-incompatible-daemon
notes:
BLOCK preflight/implementation 2026-09-09: pinned public @getpaseo/client 0.8.0-beta.1 exposes connect/state/config/providers but not connected daemon serverId or server_info. npm @getpaseo/cli status JSON obtains serverId via getOrCreateServerId(local home), while connected daemon probe returns version/status only; therefore it cannot prove selected WebSocket identity equals local CLI status without forbidden internal/raw protocol API. Local installed Paseo is 0.7.2 and was not touched. Requires owner-approved design/API delta before safe implementation.
RESOLVED 2026-09-09 by Repository owner: accept weaker local home/PID/UID/listen/version admission, keep remote targets rejected, bind manifest/lock to canonical local home plus normalized status listen, re-probe under lock, and verify immediately after mutation. Technical Design and Implementation Plan updated.
DONE 2026-09-09: Implemented canonical local-home/PID/UID/listen admission, endpoint identity hash, equal semver floor, bounded sanitized status probe, authenticated public SDK handshake/cleanup, strict preflight preventing upstream identity/config repairs and remote contact, and provider-free password containment. R2 final review PASS. Verified npm run verify (322 tests, build, pack, package test) and two isolated @getpaseo/cli 0.8.0-beta.1 handshakes including password auth; bytes/modes preserved. Accepted residual: upstream status changes server-id/config ctime metadata and connected peer identity remains unproven by public SDK.
close_reason: Definition of Done verified; final R2 security review approved

title: Recover interrupted transactions and preserve partial uninstalls
description:
## Objective
Implement dry-run recovery classification, explicit recovery apply, commit-point reconciliation, safe uninstall, and uninstall-incomplete residual manifests.

## Context
Power loss/SIGKILL can leave a journal, and customized owned artifacts must survive uninstall without permanently losing ownership evidence.

## Scope
In scope:
- Recovery service for safely committable/reversible/divergent journals.
- Install/update manifest transaction-ID reconciliation; committed full-uninstall cleanup; conditional reverse rollback; residual manifest writes.
Out of scope:
- Force deletion or automatic recovery during normal apply.

## Components Touched
- Core recovery/uninstall logic, journal/manifest transitions, crash and customization fixtures.

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- Locked transaction orchestration must be complete.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- `recover` dry-run is read-only; only `recover --apply` mutates. Normal apply/uninstall blocks on unfinished journals.
- Crash after matching install/update manifest is committed cleanup; committed uninstall journal authorizes final manifest deletion.
- Customized files/providers are preserved and retained in an uninstall-incomplete manifest; no force option.

## Validation / Definition of Done
- Crash injection immediately before/after manifest replacement, journal commit marking, manifest deletion, and journal cleanup resolves unambiguously.
- Divergent values remain untouched with exit 4 evidence.
- Partial uninstall removes unchanged owned items, retains only unresolved ownership, exits conflict, and can later fully discharge.

## Primary Proof
Recovery commit-boundary and customized-uninstall integration matrix.

## Reversibility
Recovery itself uses the same conditional before/after checks; no whole config or divergent file is overwritten. No irreversible step is accepted.

## Provenance
Source: docs/plans/paseo-room-phase-1-implementation-plan.md#wp-005-transaction-global-lock-rollback-and-recovery
Requirements: REQ-011, REQ-012, REQ-013, REQ-014
Design refs: docs/design/platform/paseo-room.md#84-recovery-around-the-commit-point; docs/design/platform/paseo-room.md#85-uninstall-with-user-customization
notes: DONE 2026-09-09: Implemented read-only recovery classification, explicit locked recovery apply, strict journal/successor/private-bundle/manifest-sidecar validation, commit-point reconciliation, conditional provider/filesystem rollback, safe full uninstall, and uninstall-incomplete residual manifests. Added provider mutation fence evidence and no-follow transaction inspection. Recovery preserves malformed/divergent/active/ambiguous state and never retries unresolved RPCs. Partial uninstall removes only unchanged ownership, verifies registry removal before files, retains customized providers and potentially referenced files, preserves mutable children, and supports later discharge. R2 found terminal cleanup, rollback-capture, stale pre-mutation admission, malformed uninstall authority and root-fsync gaps; all remediated with targeted regressions and final R2 PASS. title: Plan deterministic install, update, verify, and uninstall operations
description:

- Property tests preserve random unrelated providers and prove normalized operation ordering/idempotency.

title: Implement private staging, journal, and atomic file mutation primitives
description:
## Objective
Implement secure transaction staging, before-image capture, fsynced journal transitions, atomic per-file publish, and conditional filesystem compensation.

## Context
Filesystem changes precede provider activation but span multiple files, so every mutation needs durable intent/evidence and safe reverse behavior after handled errors or interruption.

## Scope
In scope:
- `src/core/transaction.ts` filesystem/journal primitives, private directories/files, atomic rename/fsync, file/link before/after records, and injectable faults.
Out of scope:
- Paseo patch orchestration, global lock, and command UX.

## Components Touched
- Transaction/journal/filesystem modules and failure-injection fixtures.

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- Deterministic planner and manifest ownership models must exist.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- Roots/backups/staging are 0700; regular files/journals are 0600. Never follow links or recursively replace role containers.
- Journal is persisted before mutation and after each completed step. Atomicity is per file only.
- Compensation restores only when current still equals transaction after-value; divergence is preserved.

## Risks / Gotchas
- SIGKILL/power loss cannot run handlers; durable journal must make the state classifiable later.

## Validation / Definition of Done
- Fault injection around every file mutation yields restored old state or explicit divergent recovery state.
- Modes, fsync/rename sequencing, link metadata backup, and no credential dereference are tested.
- SIGINT/SIGTERM handler path invokes conditional compensation.

## Primary Proof
Exhaustive temporary-filesystem journal/fault matrix across every state transition.

## Reversibility
All tests use disposable roots; production primitives retain before-images and never overwrite divergence.

## Provenance
Source: docs/plans/paseo-room-phase-1-implementation-plan.md#wp-005-transaction-global-lock-rollback-and-recovery
Requirements: REQ-011, REQ-012, REQ-014, REQ-016
Design refs: docs/design/platform/paseo-room.md#33-transaction-journal; docs/design/platform/paseo-room.md#72-apply-and-rollback-flow
notes: DONE 2026-09-09: Implemented strict context-bound journal v1 and filesystem-only transactions with 0700/0600 staging/before-images, cwd-anchored no-follow child operations, journal-declared UUID same-parent captures/prepared paths, no-clobber file/link/directory publication, same-held-parent fsync, durable pending actions, conditional reverse compensation, restartable cleanup, and SIGINT/SIGTERM compensation. R2 exposed unimplementable portable atomic-replace/CAS assumption; Repository owner accepted and docs record journaled temporary absence plus same-UID private-state limits. Subsequent R2 blockers for destructive races, parent rebinding, compensation durability, orphan temps, nested removal, cleanup fsync/restart, signals, and successor validation were remediated with regression/crash matrices. Verified npm run verify: typecheck, lint, 14 files/970 tests, build, pack dry-run, package test all pass on macOS. Linux execution remains release CI evidence.
